clinical_comments: Paediatric aplastic anemia, HSCT D+/R+. C592G detected 136 days post transplant, returned to WT 199 days post transplant, and then back to C592G 385 days post transplant. Received a total of 54 days GCV and 6 days FOS. CMV-associated pancreatitits suspected. Continued FOS after resistance detected. Patient improved.

Paediatric AML, HSCT D-/R+. CMV reactivated at 19 days post transplant. Had four more recurrent CMV infections over 19.4 months. GVHD. H600L/T700A detected 1237 and 1241 days post transplant after 50 days FOS. Changed to CDV, then added GCV. T700A returned to WT when M460V/E756G detected at 1272, 1297, 1332, 1363, 1393 days post transplant.Changed to GCV and FOS at 1332 days post transplant. Received a total of 61 days GCV, 50 days FOS throughout course of infection. Developed CMV GI, retinitis, pneumonia. Treated resistance with CDV, CMV IVIG. Passed away from CMV pneumonia. Patient described in Park 2022 (Covidence 7733) and Choi 2014 (Covidence 155)

Adult CLL, unsuccessful SCT. VGCV pre-emptive therapy. Five weeks later CMV detected. Continuing CMV viral load despite VGCV, C607Y detected. Changed to FOS and CMV IVIG for possible CMV pneumonia. Bronchoscopy positive for pneymocystis (CMV negative). After 6 weeks FOS, reduced dose and then changed to VGCV. Developed CMV pneumonia, C607Y/A594V/L773V/A809V/Q578L detected, changed to high-dose GCV alongside CDV. 2 weeks later A594V disappeared and V715M detected low level. Pneumonia stabilised and improved, discharged with VGCV. CMV viral load rose quickly, C607Y/A594V/L773V/A809V/DEL981-982/N408D/C539G/A834P/P522S/D413N detected, then C607Y/A594V/DEL981-982/C539G/A809V/P522S/N408D/D413N detected 3 weeks later. CLL relapsed and ongoing CMV infection excluded for further chemotherapy or transplantation. Patient passed away.

CMV reactivation 56 days post transplant. Treated with FOS then GCV and CMV IVIG. CMV resolved and continued GCV prophylaxis. CMV reactivated and developed CMV gastritis and colitis. Post mortem showed CMV and pneumocystis carinii in BAL and L802M mutations.

Patient passed away due to aspergillosis and post mortem shows BAL CMV and aspergillus.

FOS resolved CMV and LET restarted but CMV VL increased again. LET resistance detected. FOS restarted. Patient passed away due to EBV disease

Patient immune system improved to control CMV

Adult single lung transplantation D+/R-. GCV prophylaxis for one month. 60 days post transplant, CMV detected, started GCV 2 weeks later. Treatment was interrupted after 4 weeks with negative viraemia and no symptoms. Soon CMV recurred, treated with 2 weeks of GCV. After stopping GCV again, CMV detected. A594V detected 270 days post transplant in blood. Changed to FOS, which effectively cleared CMV, but discontinued after 2 weeks due to renal toxicity. CMV recurred, treated with half dose FOS. 360 days post transplant, mycobacterium tuberculosis detected in bronchoscopy. 2 weeks later FOS discontinued with negative CMV. One week later CMV recurred, full-dose GCV commenced, but CMV remained at high-level. H520Q/P522S detected. Patient passed away shortly after due to lung failure.

clinical_comments: CMV reactivation 6 weeks post transplantation, started on FOS. FOS side-effects, so FOS/GCV combination started and CMV VL reduced. Patient developed CMV pneumonia, no resistance detected. FOS stopped at week 13 due to side-effects, GVHD developed, requiring increased immunosuppression. CMV VL increased and resistance detected. Started on CDV and ribavirin to treat CMV/Adenovirus. CDV didn't reduce CMV, so started on leflunomide and MBV, CMV reduced. Further resistance detected. Back on FOS, but CMV VL increased and CMV pneumonia relapsed. Started on higher dose of MBV, MBV/FOS/GCV resistance detected. FOS stopped, only MBV, but further MBV resistance emerged. Sequencing of clones also revealed UL97 H411N mutation, but direct sequencing did not detect this. CMV and adeno resolved. Alive.

SCID. Fullterm uncomplicated pregnancy. 4 weeks of age, failure to thrive and anemia. Presented for care at 13 weeks old. CSF grew acinetobacter baumanii. Diagnosed with SCID. Alveolar disease, CMV deteted in BAL. Repeat CMV testing on CSF found detected but below limit result. CMV retinitis. Started on GCV and IVIG with good response. Clinically improved over 6 weeks, GCV dose decreased, but day 58, viral load increased again. Day 65 GCV increased. CMV continued to increase, FOS started day 74. VL reduced in one week. M460V/M460I/A594V detected day 86. HSCT performed dat 115, GCV discontinued day 117 due to resistance detection and potential GCV-myelosuppression. Neurologic status decreased and GCV restarted alongside CDV for presumed CMV encephalitis. L595S detected in blood and M460I/M460V in urine at day 136. CSF WT. Neurologic status improved, and VL reduced. No evidence of marrow engraftment. Day 210, respiratory distress, and respiratory failure on day 212. Multiorgan failure 219. L595S/K513N/T700A detected day 219. CMV pneumonitis. Despite GCV, FOS, CDV, passed away day 228.

4 month old, failure to thrive, presumed immunodeficiency, CMV detected in blood. Treated with GCV. MHC class II deficiency diagnosed. 4 weeks later GCV dose frequency reduced, but CMV VL increased and regular dosing resumed. VL continued to increase, switched to FOS and CMV IVIG. M460V detected in nasopharangeal aspirate (NPA), CSF and blood. Patient deteriorated, despite treatment and developed CMV encephalitis. HSCT performed D+/R+. Possible central CMV infection, CDV added to FOS. M460V/DEL981-982 detected in blood and NPA at 1 day post transplant. 13 days post transplant respiratory symptoms exacerbated, CDV stopped due to cytopenia and increased viral load. 19 days post transplant M460V had reverted to WT, but DEL981-982 still detected. Clinical deterioration of respiratory and liver function and uncontrollable sepsis, started on palliative care. DEL981-982 detected in blood NPA and urine up to 33 days post transplant. Patient passed away 36 days post transplant with encephalitis, respiratory and cardiac arrest.

Patient passed away after multiple complications at 18 months post transplant.

Adult, HIV, CMV retinitis. Treated with GCV for 21 days, then VGCV. Retinitis resolved. 2 years later (continuing VGCV) CMV retinitis returned. L595S detected. Changed to FOS for 21 days, VGCV. VGCV-induced myelosuppression so discontinued VGCV. CD4 count increased so stopped CMV treatment. Alive

Adult diabetes, kidney and pancreas D+/R-. Half dose prophylaxis due to renal insufficiency (GCV then VGCV). 10 weeks post transplant while on VGCV, developed CMV posthitis. CMV CTL's and IVIG. CMV resolved and VGCV stopped 34 weeks post transplantation. 13 months post transplant CMV reoccurred with CMV colitis. 10 days GCV, with clinical improvement. 6 weeks later symptomatic, but low VL. High-dose GCV for 2 weeks with clinical improvement, but colitis persisted. Resistance detected. Retrospective testing identified mutations from 13 months post transplant. Did not want to change to potentially nephrotoxic antiviral treatment, so removed GCV and treated with IVIG and CTLs. 20 months post transplantation colitis resolved. Alive
participant_desc: Solid Organ Transplant; Other: Pancreas and Kidney

clinical_comments: Presented with CMV colitis and retinitis initially treated with GCV, but changed to FOS due to no response. Resistance detected in plasma and colonic biopsies. CMV IVIG added. FOS side-effects , but CMV reduced. Started on LET prophylaxis. Some fluctuations of CMV VL on LET, but no CMV disease. After 11 weeks of LT, CMV reactivated, resistance detected. Changed back to FOS and CMV reduced. Two more reactivations controlled with FOS, C325Y mutation persisted 20 weeks after stopping LET so could not change back to LET.

clinical_comments: HSCT, 6 months post transplant had 3 episodes of CMV treated with GCV then VGCV. VGCV prophylaxis continued after third reactivation. 8 months post transplant CMV VL increased, VGCV changed to GCV, CMV persisted after 6 weeks GCV so dose increased. Decision made to discontinue further treatment and patient passed away.

3month old respiratory failure due to CMV and PCP. MHC class II deficiency requiring HSCT. PCP resolved, but CMV persisted. Treated with GCV. CMV persisted, treated with FOS. CMV resolved 4 weeks later and FOS continued. CNS symptoms developed, CMV and HHV6 negative in CSF. CMV VL returned despite FOS. FOS increased but failed to reduce VL. Resistance testing performed. FOS CDV leflunomide and artesunate started. Transplant performed. 2 weeks later, changed to GCV. CDV weekly for 2 weeks then biweekly, leflunomide and art esunate continued. CMV VL continued to rise. UL54 mutation results. Letermovir added to GCV, leflunomide and artsunate. CMV resolved. Possibly developed drug-induced lung injury and passed away 5 months post transplant.

59yo chronic kidney disease. VGCV prophylaxis for 3 months post transplant. 4 months post developed CMV 350000 IU/mL. Treated with GCV adjusted to renal function. Alive.

1yo, D-/R+. CMV reactivated 17 days post transplant. Treated with FOS then switch to GCV. CMV resolved but relapsed day 61, adjusted immunosuppression. A594V mutation detected. CMV T-cells on day 47 with continuing FOS> Retinitis resolved and CMV VL reduced. Leukemia relapsed and GVHD developed. CMV worsened, FOS continued until day 257. Changed to LET off-label. Passed away day 336 due to refractory disease.

C325R detected day 52 (2 weeks before Sanger). C325R became dominant strain by day 67. C325R also found in BAL. CMV VL reduced, changed to VGCV after 3 weeks. Continued decrease. Started on FOS and MBV which resolved CMV. MBV shortage for 3 weeks caused relapse of CMV, but resolved again. MBV continued after 12 months without CMV relapse. Alive.
